question: What is the Photon engine?
options: A storage format like Parquet
A scheduling service
A native, vectorized C++ query engine that accelerates Spark SQL and DataFrame workloads
A notebook language
explanation: Photon is Databricks' native, vectorized execution engine written in C++ that speeds up SQL and DataFrame operations while remaining compatible with Spark APIs.

question: Why can Photon outperform the default JVM-based Spark execution?
options: It runs on the driver only
It skips reading the data
It uses vectorized processing and native code to better exploit modern CPUs
It removes all transformations
explanation: Photon processes data in vectorized batches using optimized native code, leveraging CPU SIMD and cache efficiency to outperform row-at-a-time JVM execution for many workloads.

question: Which workloads benefit most from Photon?
options: Only single-row lookups
SQL, aggregations, joins, and Delta writes
Only UDF-heavy Python loops
Nothing benefits
explanation: Photon accelerates SQL queries, aggregations, joins, and Delta operations; benefits are largest for scan- and compute-heavy analytical workloads.

question: What is a cost consideration when enabling Photon?
options: Photon-enabled compute has a higher DBU rate, so you weigh speedup against increased per-hour cost
Photon is always free with no DBU impact
Photon deletes data to save money
Photon disables autoscaling
explanation: Photon carries a higher DBU multiplier, so the trade-off is whether the runtime speedup lowers total cost enough to justify the higher hourly rate.

question: How compatible is Photon with existing Spark code?
options: You must rewrite everything in C++
It is API-compatible; supported operations are transparently accelerated, unsupported ones fall back to Spark
It requires a new query language
It only supports Scala
explanation: Photon is a drop-in accelerator: supported operators run natively and unsupported ones gracefully fall back to standard Spark, so existing code works unchanged.
